content: Pulmonary toilet, also known as pulmonary hygiene, refers to a collection of techniques aimed at clearing mucus and secretions from the airways. The term pulmonary pertains to the lungs, while toilet originates from the French word toilette, which relates to body care and hygiene, as seen in words like toiletry that are associated with cleansing. Pulmonary toilet serves to prevent atelectasis, which is the collapse of the alveoli in the lungs. It also helps to eliminate secretions from the respiratory system that could otherwise lead to respiratory infections. Additionally, it can reduce pulmonary shunting, enhance the functional reserve capacity of the lungs, and prevent respiratory infections following chest trauma. Various methods are employed in pulmonary toilet. These include suctioning to remove fluids and positioning the patient in ways that allow secretions to drain by gravity. Techniques such as airway suctioning, chest physiotherapy, the use of blow bottles, and nasotracheal suction are commonly utilized. Bronchoscopy, a procedure in which a tube is inserted into the airways to allow visualization, can also be used therapeutically as part of pulmonary toilet. Incentive spirometry and the administration of analgesics that do not suppress breathing are integral components of pulmonary hygiene. Coughing is another critical mechanism for clearing secretions from the airways. Therefore, healthcare providers take care not to oversedate patients, as this could inhibit their ability to cough effectively. Tracheotomy, a surgical procedure to create an opening in the trachea, can facilitate pulmonary toilet. Percussion, a technique involving rhythmic tapping on the chest, helps to loosen secretions and enables the cilia in the airways to remove material. Positioning is another important method for promoting the drainage of secretions. For instance, patients may be placed in a prone position to aid in this process. Pulmonary toilet is applied in various clinical scenarios. It is used to prevent infections such as pneumonia and to manage conditions like pneumonia and cystic fibrosis. For individuals with chronic lung diseases, pulmonary hygiene is essential for preventing infections and lung abscesses. Furthermore, it is employed to prevent acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) following chest trauma.
